clue.text: Church girl's cup

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name; the 's is just a link

explanation.surface: A church's girl and her cup, perhaps at communion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially the communion cup used in church services.

clue.text: Beginning of Hamlet's speech not finished by friend

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from the next word
something not finished lacks its final letter, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Hamlet's opening speech left incomplete by his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in Shakespeare's play, so the name stands for that friend.

clue.text: See 16
9's outside mine where there's no main drainage

indicators.note: only the outside portions of the cross-referenced answer are kept, dropping its interior letters

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer to 9 down, the chess meetings
a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit

explanation.surface: Something outside a mine in a place with no mains sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is a cross-reference to another answer in the grid; 'outside' keeps only its outer parts, the opening letter and the closing three.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit collects sewage where a house is not connected to a main drain or sewer.

clue.text: Woman to summon return of old record

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: return means the following word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to call someone is to summon them

explanation.surface: A woman summons the return of an old gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: Old 78 rpm gramophone records were pressed from shellac, so the material names the record.

clue.text: Name for spinach and lettuce

indicators.note: for signals that the letters standing for the answer lie within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A salad-garden question about what to call spinach and lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across spinacH AND LEttuce; the salad leaves are pure camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or nickname, as in a radio user's handle.

clue.text: The watch (incorrect French and English) will provide answer

parts.note: le is French for the, here wrongly used with a feminine noun
montre is the French word for a watch

explanation.surface: A garbled French phrase for the watch, plus English, supplies the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In correct French it is LA montre, so 'incorrect French' excuses LE. The definition puns on Will Holt, who wrote the folk song of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon Tree is the folk song written by Will Holt, so it is the answer Will provided.

clue.text: Insectivorous insect with no name eating the larger insects initially

indicators.note: eating means the first piece swallows the second, which ends up inside it

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, describes a work with no name attached

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A nameless insect-eater devours the initial bigger insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no name' is the clue's definition-looking trap: it is a synonym for nameless, and 'eating' swallows three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The antlion larva traps and eats ants and other small insects in a sand pit.

clue.text: Board meetings for 16s (15) at a time

definitions.text: Board meetings for 16s (15) at a time

parts.words: Board meetings for 16s (15) at a time
parts.note: 16 and 15 combine as grand plus two-master, i.e. grandmasters meeting two at a time over a chess board

explanation.walkthrough: Read 16s (15) as the answers to 16 across and 15 down: GRAND and TWO-MASTER suggest grandmasters, who play in pairs, two at a time, across a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess congress is a tournament gathering where players compete in pairs across boards.

clue.text: Girl's lost in network

indicators.note: lost means the following word is taken away from the name

parts.note: Ingrid is a girl's name; the 's reads as has
the word in is the letters removed

explanation.surface: A girl gets lost somewhere in a network.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of crossing lines, such as an electricity distribution system.

clue.text: Death's head, for example, makes a riddler largely mum

parts.note: the Sphinx of Greek myth posed riddles to travellers

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, its ending cut off

parts.note: mum is the familiar name for mother

explanation.surface: The Death's head, a riddler who keeps mostly quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like silent; it is mother, and 'largely' trims it to MOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The death's-head hawkmoth is a sphinx moth, named for the skull-like pattern on its thorax.

clue.text: See 25
Fish with no means of identifying coil

parts.note: sole is a flatfish
taken as written
ID stands for identification, a means of identifying someone

explanation.surface: A fish without any way to identify a coil.
explanation.definitionFit: A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire that acts as a magnet when current flows.

clue.text: Cheer for scented plant with underground source

parts.note: to root for a team is to cheer for it
stock is a sweet-scented garden flower

explanation.surface: A gardener cheering on a scented plant that grows from underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootstock is the underground stem or root system from which new growth springs.

clue.text: Company director's ketch?

parts.note: from the saying two's company
a master directs others, as in master of ceremonies; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A company director's yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company director' reads as one businessman; split it, as in the saying two's company, three's a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a sailing boat with two masts, the mizzen shorter than the main.

clue.text: Principals on the square avert danger with gold

indicators.note: to avert is to turn away, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Leaders head off danger with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the square' is Masonic slang for being a Freemason, so the definition means Masonic principals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Lodge is the governing body of a Masonic jurisdiction, its senior principals.

clue.text: Exclusive ice cream server

definitions.meaning: a news story one paper has that others do not
a ladle-like spoon for serving rounded portions of ice cream

explanation.definitionFit: Scoop means both a newspaper exclusive and the utensil for serving ice cream.

clue.text: Cavil — there's nothing right with cover for wheels

parts.note: to carp is to cavil or find petty fault
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Grumbling that there is nothing right about a shelter for the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is an open-sided shelter that covers a parked car.

clue.text: Pull from funnel set in ice

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the frozen water
set means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Trying to pull a funnel that is frozen in ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' looks like a physical tug; it means clout. 'set' scrambles the funnel and 'in' freezes it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pull, in the sense of clout or sway over others, is influence.

clue.text: Light left before fleet

parts.note: ante is Latin for before
RN, the Royal Navy, is Britain's fleet

explanation.surface: A light on the left ahead of the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable light in a protective case.

clue.text: Davy had no time for architectural ornament

indicators.note: had no means one letter is removed from the surname

parts.note: Davy Crockett, the American frontiersman

explanation.surface: The frontiersman had no time for architectural decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had no' drops one T from CROCKETT.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocket is a carved leaf-like knob decorating gothic spires and gables.

clue.text: Fellow on line displays nonconformity

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
the El is an elevated railway line in Chicago

explanation.surface: A man on a railway line shows his rebellious streak.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. In Britain 'chapel' stands for nonconformist Protestantism, as against church.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapel is used collectively for nonconformist worship, as in church versus chapel in Wales.

clue.text: Break a lung

definitions.meaning: an organ that draws breath, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a rest, and literally something that breathes, as a lung does.

clue.text: Hunter finding game with stick

parts.note: nim is a mathematical game of removing counters
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A hunter finding prey with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests quarry; it is the counter game NIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name means any great hunter.

clue.text: Actor's line in film studios covered by politician

indicators.note: covered by means everything else sits inside the politician's letters

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament

indicators.note: in puts the line inside the studio name

parts.note: Elstree is a famous film studio complex north of London
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An actor's line delivered at the film studios is hushed up by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' and 'in' nest a railway line inside the studio and the studio inside the politician. 'Actor's' reads as Actor is.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is the American film actress, famed for her many Oscar nominations.

clue.text: As well over in the ivory cleaner

parts.note: too means as well

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the word the

parts.note: past means over, as in the danger is past

explanation.surface: Also left over in the ivory cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothpaste cleans the teeth, jocularly called ivories.

clue.text: Debauchee inclined to be a gatherer

definitions.meaning: a garden tool for gathering leaves

explanation.surface: A libertine with a tendency to collect things.
explanation.definitionFit: Rake means both a dissolute man and the toothed garden tool for gathering leaves.

clue.text: Leading light let out to give alarm

parts.note: a star is a leading light, a prominent performer

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A star is released to raise the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give someone a sudden fright or alarm.

clue.text: Put air into home at boring point

parts.note: in means at home
flat means dull or boring
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: Putting air in at home when things are dull.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate a tyre or balloon is to fill it with air.
